skills.name: Atmospheric pressure and the simple barometer

note.text:
The atmosphere is a layer of air around the Earth; its weight presses on everything: this is atmospheric pressure, about 100 000 Pa (100 kPa) at sea level.
Demonstrations: a can crushes when the air inside is removed (by steam then cooling); a card stays on an upturned glass of water; a straw works because the air pushes the drink up.
The simple mercury barometer: a tube full of mercury is upturned in a dish; the mercury falls until about 760 mm (0.76 m) is left. The air pressure holds up that column: p = ρgh.
Mercury is used because it is very dense (13 600 kg/m³), so the tube can be short; a water barometer would need about 10 m.

sections.heading: An ocean of air
sections.text:
We live at the bottom of an ocean of air many kilometres deep. That air has weight, and it presses on everything: this is atmospheric pressure, about {100000} Pa at sea level.
We do not feel it because the fluids in our body push outwards just as hard.

sections.heading: Seeing it work
sections.text:
• Boil a little water in a can, close it and cool it: the steam turns back to water, the pressure inside drops, and the outside air crushes the can.
• A straw: you lower the pressure inside; the air pushes the drink up.
• A full glass with a card on top can be turned over without spilling: the air holds up the card.

sections.heading: The mercury barometer
sections.text:
Fill a long glass tube with mercury, close the end and turn it upside down into a dish of mercury. The mercury falls until the column is about {760} mm high, leaving a vacuum at the top.
The air pressure on the dish holds up the column, so p = ρgh = {13600} × {10} × {0.76} ≈ {103360} Pa.
Mercury is used because it is so dense; with water the tube would need to be about {10} m tall.

key_words.meaning: the pressure caused by the weight of the air
an instrument that measures atmospheric pressure

examples: A water barometer needs about {10} m of water

mistake.wrong: A straw sucks the drink up
mistake.right: The air pushes the drink up when the pressure in the straw is lowered
mistake.why: Suction is not a pulling force: atmospheric pressure does the work.

cards.idea: The weight of the air above us causes atmospheric pressure, about {100} kPa.
example: A can crushes when the air inside is removed.

cards.idea: A barometer's mercury column is held up by air pressure: p = ρgh.
Mercury is used because it is dense: the column is short.
example: Water would need a tube about {10} m tall.

pick.q: Why is mercury used in a barometer rather than water?
pick.r: Mercury is very dense, so the column is short (about 76 cm)
w: Water evaporates too fast to read
e: Mercury is expensive.
The main reason is the height: water would need about 10 m.
Mercury is about 13.6 times denser than water.
pick.y: p = ρgh: a large ρ gives a small h.

pick.q: What is in the space above the mercury in a barometer tube?
e: Air would push the mercury down and spoil the reading.
No water is in the tube.
There is only a tiny amount of mercury vapour.
pick.y: The tube was full of mercury before it was turned over; nothing replaced the mercury that fell.

pick.q: If the barometer tube is tilted, what happens to the vertical height of the mercury column?
e: The mercury fills more of the tube, but the vertical height is fixed by air pressure.
Air pressure has not changed.
Air pressure still holds the mercury up.
pick.y: Only the vertical height depends on the air pressure.

pick.q: Steam fills a can, the lid is closed and the can is cooled. It collapses. Why?
pick.r: The steam condenses, the pressure inside falls, and the air outside crushes the can
w: The steam pulls the walls in
e: Cooling the metal this little does not crush it.
Steam does not pull; the outside air pushes.
Its weight barely changes.
pick.y: Atmospheric pressure outside is much larger than the pressure left inside.

pick.q: How does a drinking straw work?
pick.r: You lower the pressure in the straw; atmospheric pressure pushes the drink up
w: Your mouth pulls the drink up by suction force
The drink is lighter than air
e: Suction is not a force: the outside air does the pushing.
Drinks are much denser than air.
The straw does not squeeze anything.
pick.y: Air pressure on the surface of the drink pushes it up the straw.

pick.q: A card covers a full glass of water turned upside down, and the water does not fall. Why?
pick.r: Atmospheric pressure on the card is greater than the water pressure on it
w: The card is glued by the water
e: Water does not glue strongly enough to hold the weight.
Water has weight.
Glass is not magnetic.
pick.y: The air pushes up on the card with about {100000} Pa.

questions.prompt: At sea level in Limbe a barometer reads {760} mm of mercury; at the top of a hill it reads {r} mm. Find the difference in atmospheric pressure (Pa).

misconceptions.explain: That is the pressure at the top. The question asks for the difference.

solution: Difference in height = {760} − {r} = {760 - r} mm = {(760 - r) / 1000} m.
